info.title: OptiTech API
info.description:
The OptiTech API allows you to access and manage OptiTech programmatically. You can use the OptiTech API to manage API keys, programs, frameworks, integrations, registers, roles, and operations. For information about these features, refer to the [OptiTech documentation](/docs/manage/overview/).

You can run OptiTech API requests from this API reference using the **Try It** feature. Enter your API key as a **Bearer** token in the **Authorization** section of the page.

You can create and manage API keys in the OptiTech Console. See [Manage API keys](/docs/manage/api-keys/) for instructions.

get.description:
Analyzes the register for security and performance issues.
Returns a list of issues categorized by severity (ERROR, WARN, INFO).

Requires read access to the program and Data API enabled.

parameters.name: framework_id
parameters.description: Framework ID to analyze. If not specified, the program's default framework is used.

parameters.name: register_name
parameters.description: Register name to analyze. Required if framework has multiple registers.

parameters.name: min_severity
parameters.description: Minimum severity level to include. For example, WARN returns WARN and ERROR issues, excluding INFO.

200.description: Successfully retrieved security advisor issues

get.description:
Retrieves the API keys for your OptiTech account.
The response does not include API key tokens. A token is only provided when creating an API key.
API keys can also be managed in the OptiTech Console.
For more information, see [Manage API keys](/docs/manage/api-keys/).

200.description: Returned the API keys for the OptiTech account

post.description:
Creates an API key.
The `key_name` is a user-specified name for the key.
Returns an `id` and `key`; the `key` is a randomly generated, 64-bit token required to access the OptiTech API.
Store the key securely — it is only returned once.
API keys can also be managed in the OptiTech Console.
See [Manage API keys](/docs/manage/api-keys/).

200.description: Created an API key

delete.description:
Revokes the specified API key.
An API key that is no longer needed can be revoked.
This action cannot be reversed.
API keys can also be managed in the OptiTech Console.
See [Manage API keys](/docs/manage/api-keys/).

200.description: Revoked the specified API key

get.description:
Retrieves details for the specified operation.
An operation is an action performed on an OptiTech program resource.

200.description: Returned details for the specified operation

get.description:
Retrieves a list of programs for the specified organization.
If using a personal API key, include the `org_id` parameter to specify which organization to work with.
If using an org API key, `org_id` is automatically inferred from the key.
For more information, see [Manage organizations using the OptiTech API](/docs/manage/orgs-api)
and [Manage programs](/docs/manage/programs/).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Specify the cursor value from the previous response to retrieve the next batch of programs.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Specify a value from 1 to 400 to limit number of programs in the response.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Search by program `name` or `id`. You can specify partial `name` or `id` values to filter results.

parameters.name: recoverable
parameters.description: Show only deleted programs within the recovery window.

200.description: Returned a list of programs for the OptiTech account

post.description:
Creates an OptiTech program within an organization.
If using a personal API key, include the `org_id` parameter to specify which organization to create the program in.
If using an org API key, `org_id` is automatically inferred from the key.
Plan limits define how many programs you can create.
For more information, see [Manage programs](/docs/manage/programs/).

You can specify a region and Postgres version in the request body.
Neon currently supports PostgreSQL 14, 15, 16, 17, and 18.
For supported regions and `region_id` values, see [Regions](/docs/introduction/regions/).

get.description:
Retrieves a list of programs shared with your OptiTech account.
For more information, see [Manage programs](/docs/manage/programs/).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Specify the cursor value from the previous response to get the next batch of programs.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Specify a value from 1 to 400 to limit number of programs in the response.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Search query by name or id.

200.description: Returned a list of shared programs for the OptiTech account

get.description:
Retrieves information about the specified program.
Returned details include the program settings, compute configuration, history retention, owner information, and current usage metrics.

200.description: Returned information about the specified program

patch.description:
Updates the specified program.
Configurable properties include the program name, default compute settings, history retention period, and IP allowlist.

200.description: Updated the specified program

delete.description:
Deletes the specified program and all its endpoints, frameworks, registers, and users.
Deleted programs can be recovered within 7 days using `POST /programs/{program_id}/recover`.
To list recoverable programs, use `GET /programs?recoverable=true`.

200.description: Deleted the specified program

post.description:
Recovers a deleted program within the 7-day deletion recovery period.
Restores frameworks, endpoints, settings, and connection strings.
Some integrations require manual reconfiguration after recovery.
To list recoverable programs, use `GET /programs?recoverable=true`.

200.description: Returned the recovered program

get.description:
Retrieves a list of operations for the specified OptiTech program.
The number of operations returned can be large.
To paginate the response, issue an initial request with a `limit` value.
Then, add the `cursor` value that was returned in the response to the next request.
Operations older than 6 months may be deleted from our systems.
If you need more history than that, you should store your own history.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Specify the cursor value from the previous response to get the next batch of operations

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Specify a value from 1 to 1000 to limit number of operations in the response

get.description: Retrieves details about users who have access to the program, including the permission `id`, the granted-to email address, and the date program access was granted.

200.description: Returned program access details

post.description: Grants program access to the account associated with the specified email address.

200.description: Granted program access

delete.description: Revokes program access from the user associated with the specified permission `id`. You can retrieve a user's permission `id` by listing program access.

200.description: Revoked program access

get.description:
Returns the shared preload libraries available for the specified program's Postgres version.
Shared preload libraries are Postgres extensions that require the `shared_preload_libraries`
setting and a compute restart to activate.
Use this list to determine which libraries can be enabled in the program's
`settings.preload_libraries` configuration.

200.description: Successfully returned available shared preload libraries

post.description:
Creates a transfer request for the specified program. The request expires after a set period.
To accept the request, the recipient calls `PUT /programs/{program_id}/transfer_requests/{request_id}`
or uses the OptiTech Console claim link.
The optional `ru` parameter redirects the recipient after acceptance.

ttl_seconds.description:
Specifies the validity duration of the transfer request in seconds. If not provided,
the request will expire after 24 hours (86,400 seconds).

parameters.name: request_id
parameters.description: The OptiTech program transfer request ID

put.description:
Accepts a transfer request for the specified program, transferring it to the specified organization
or user. If org_id is not passed, the program will be transferred to the current user or organization account.

org_id.description:
The OptiTech organization ID to transfer the program to. If not provided, the program will be
transferred to the current user or organization account.

406.description: Account doesn't satisfy the plan requirements to own the program

get.description: Returns the JWKS URLs available for verifying JWTs used as the authentication mechanism for the specified program.

200.description: The JWKS URLs available for the program

post.description:
Adds a JWKS URL to the specified program for verifying JWTs used as the authentication mechanism.

The URL must be a valid HTTPS URL that returns a JSON Web Key Set.

The `provider_name` field allows you to specify which authentication provider you're using (e.g., Clerk, Auth0, AWS Cognito).

The `framework_id` scopes the JWKS URL to specific frameworks; if not specified, it applies to all frameworks.

The `role_names` scopes the URL to specific roles; if not specified, default roles are used (`authenticator`, `authenticated`, `anonymous`).

The `jwt_audience` specifies which `aud` values are accepted in JWTs.

201.description: The JWKS URL was added to the program's authentication connections

delete.description:
Removes the specified JWKS URL from the program.
JWTs signed by keys from the removed URL can no longer authenticate to the program's endpoints.

200.description: Deleted a JWKS URL from the program

post.description:
Creates a new instance of OptiTech Data API in the specified framework.
The Data API exposes a REST interface over the framework register. The `register_name` path parameter determines which register the API serves.

patch.description:
Updates the OptiTech Data API configuration for the specified framework.
You can optionally provide settings to update the Data API configuration.
The schema cache is always refreshed as part of this operation.

201.description: Updated the OptiTech Data API configuration and refreshed the schema cache

delete.description:
Deletes the OptiTech Data API for the specified framework.
Existing connections using the Data API endpoint will fail after deletion.

200.description: Deleted the OptiTech Data API for the specified framework

get.description:
Retrieves the OptiTech Data API configuration for the specified framework,
including endpoint URL, enabled state, and register settings.

200.description: Returns the OptiTech Data API for the specified framework

post.description:
DEPRECATED, use `/programs/{program_id}/frameworks/{framework_id}/auth` instead. Creates a program on a third-party authentication provider's platform for use with OptiTech Auth.
Use this endpoint if the frontend integration flow can't be used.

get.summary: Retrieve OptiTech Auth details for the framework
get.description:
Retrieves the OptiTech Auth integration details for the specified framework,
including the auth provider type and integration status.

200.description: Fetched the details of the OptiTech Auth integration for the specified framework

post.summary: Enable OptiTech Auth for the framework
post.description:
Enables OptiTech Auth for the specified framework by connecting it to an authentication provider.
Creating the integration provisions the `neon_auth` schema in the framework register, which stores user identity data synchronized from the provider.

201.description: Enables OptiTech Auth integration for the framework

delete.summary: Disable OptiTech Auth for the framework
delete.description:
Disables the OptiTech Auth integration for the specified framework, removing the connection
to the authentication provider.
If `delete_data` is `true`, also deletes the `neon_auth` schema and all associated tables
from the framework register.
The integration can be re-enabled by calling `POST /programs/{program_id}/frameworks/{framework_id}/auth`.

delete_data.description: If true, deletes the `neon_auth` schema from the register

200.description: Delete the integration with the authentication provider

200.description: Returned the domains in the redirect_uri whitelist

post.description: DEPRECATED, use `/programs/{program_id}/frameworks/{framework_id}/auth/domains` instead. Adds a domain to the redirect_uri whitelist for the specified program.

201.description: Added the domain to the redirect_uri whitelist

delete.description: DEPRECATED, use `/programs/{program_id}/frameworks/{framework_id}/auth/domains` instead. Deletes a domain from the redirect_uri whitelist for the specified program.

200.description: Deleted the domain from the redirect_uri whitelist

get.description:
Lists the trusted domains in the redirect URI whitelist for the specified framework.
Only domains in this list are permitted as redirect targets after authentication.

200.description: Returned the domains in the redirect_uri whitelist

post.description:
Adds a domain to the redirect URI whitelist for the specified framework.
Only domains in this list are permitted as redirect targets after authentication.

201.description: Added the domain to the redirect_uri whitelist

delete.description:
Removes a domain from the redirect URI whitelist for the specified framework.
After removal, the domain can no longer be used as a redirect target after authentication.

200.description: Deleted the domain from the redirect_uri whitelist

post.description:
Generates SDK or API Keys for the auth provider. These might be called different things depending
on the auth provider you're using, but are generally used for setting up the frontend and backend SDKs.

DEPRECATED, use `/programs/{program_id}/frameworks/{framework_id}/auth/users` instead. Creates a new user in OptiTech Auth.
The user will be created in your neon_auth.users_sync table and automatically propagated to your auth program, whether OptiTech-managed or provider-owned.

Creates a new user in the OptiTech Auth user directory for the specified framework.
The user is created in the `neon_auth.users_sync` table and can immediately authenticate
using the framework's configured auth providers.

delete.description:
Deletes the specified user from the OptiTech Auth user directory for the specified framework.
Removes the user record from `neon_auth.users_sync`. This action cannot be undone.

put.description:
Updates the role of a user in the OptiTech Auth user directory for the specified framework.
The role controls the user's level of access within the OptiTech Auth integration.

200.description: Updated the auth user role

delete.description: DEPRECATED, use `/programs/{program_id}/frameworks/{framework_id}/auth/users/{auth_user_id}` instead. Deletes the auth user for the specified program.

post.summary: Transfer OptiTech-managed auth program to your own account
post.description: Transfers ownership of your OptiTech-managed auth program to your own auth provider account.

200.description: Transfer initiated. Follow the URL to complete the process in your auth provider's UI.

get.summary: List active integrations with auth providers
get.description: DEPRECATED, use `/programs/{program_id}/frameworks/{framework_id}/auth` instead.

200.description: Return management API keys metadata

get.description: DEPRECATED, use `/programs/{program_id}/frameworks/{framework_id}/auth/oauth_providers` instead. Lists the OAuth providers for the specified program.

200.description: Returns the OAuth providers for the OptiTech Auth

200.description: The OAuth provider has been added to the program

200.description: The OAuth provider has been added to the program

200.description: The OAuth provider has been added to the program

200.description: Deleted the OAuth provider from the program

patch.description: Updates a OAuth provider for the specified program.

200.description: The OAuth provider has been added to the program

delete.description: Deletes a OAuth provider from the specified program.

200.description: Deleted the OAuth provider from the program

200.description: Returns the email server configuration for the OptiTech Auth

patch.description: DEPRECATED, use `/programs/{program_id}/frameworks/{framework_id}/auth/email_provider` instead. Updates the email server configuration for the specified program.

200.description: The OAuth provider has been added to the program

Sends a test email using the configured email server settings to verify SMTP connectivity and credentials.
The request body must include the SMTP server settings
(`host`, `port`, `username`, `password`, `sender_email`, `sender_name`) and the `recipient_email` address.

200.description: Response with the result of the test email send

get.description:
Retrieves the email and password authentication configuration for the specified framework's OptiTech Auth integration,
including whether it is enabled and the email verification method.

200.description: Returns the email and password configuration for OptiTech Auth

patch.description:
Updates the email and password authentication configuration for the specified framework's OptiTech Auth integration.
Only the fields provided in the request body are updated.

200.description: The email and password configuration has been updated

get.description:
Retrieves the email provider configuration for the specified framework's OptiTech Auth integration,
including the provider type and server settings.

200.description: Returns the email provider configuration for the OptiTech Auth

patch.description:
Updates the email provider configuration for the specified framework's OptiTech Auth integration.
The email provider handles transactional messages such as verification emails and password reset links.

200.description: The email provider configuration has been updated

delete.description: DEPRECATED, use `/programs/{program_id}/frameworks/{framework_id}/auth` instead.

delete_data.description: If true, deletes the `neon_auth` schema from the register

200.description: Delete the integration with the authentication provider

get.description:
Retrieves a connection URI for the specified register.
The URI uses the standard PostgreSQL connection string format. Set `pooled=true` to include the `-pooler` suffix for a connection pooler URI.

parameters.name: framework_id
parameters.description: The framework ID. Defaults to your program's default `framework_id` if not specified.

parameters.name: integration_id
parameters.description: The endpoint ID. Defaults to the read-write `integration_id` associated with the `framework_id` if not specified.

parameters.name: pooled
parameters.description: Adds the `-pooler` option to the connection URI when set to `true`, creating a pooled connection URI.

200.description: Returned the connection URI

get.description:
Retrieves the localhost allow setting for the specified framework's OptiTech Auth integration.
When enabled, authentication flows work from `localhost` without adding it to the redirect URI whitelist.

200.description: The allow localhost configuration

patch.description:
Updates the localhost allow setting for the specified framework's OptiTech Auth integration.
When enabled, authentication flows work from `localhost` without adding it to the redirect URI whitelist.

200.description: Updated the allow localhost configuration

get.description:
Returns all plugin configurations for OptiTech Auth in a single response.
This endpoint aggregates organization, email provider, email and password,
OAuth providers, and localhost settings.

200.description: Returns all plugin configurations

patch.description:
Updates the organization plugin configuration for OptiTech Auth.
The organization plugin enables multi-tenant organization support.

200.description: The organization plugin configuration has been updated

patch.description:
Updates the auth configuration for the framework.
Currently supports updating the application name used in auth emails.

200.description: The auth configuration has been updated

patch.description:
Updates the magic link plugin configuration for OptiTech Auth.
The magic link plugin enables passwordless authentication via email magic links.

200.description: The magic link plugin configuration has been updated

get.description:
Returns the phone number plugin configuration for OptiTech Auth.
The phone number plugin enables phone-based OTP authentication.

200.description: Returns the phone number plugin configuration

patch.description:
Updates the phone number plugin configuration for OptiTech Auth.
Only the fields provided in the request body are updated; omitted fields retain their current values.
The phone number plugin enables phone-based OTP authentication.
OTP codes are delivered via the `send.otp` webhook event with `delivery_preference: "sms"`.
A webhook must be configured with the `send.otp` event enabled for SMS delivery to work.

200.description: The phone number plugin configuration has been updated

get.description:
Returns the webhook configuration for the specified framework's OptiTech Auth integration,
including the endpoint URL and the events that trigger it.

200.description: Returns webhook configuration for OptiTech Auth

put.description:
Updates the webhook configuration for the specified framework's OptiTech Auth integration.
Webhooks notify an external endpoint when auth events occur, such as user creation or sign-in.

200.description: Returns the updated webhook configuration

post.description:
Creates a framework in the specified program.
No request body is required, but you can specify one to create an integration or select a non-default parent framework.
By default, the framework is created from the program's default framework with no integration, and the framework name is auto-generated.
To access the framework, add a `read_write` integration.
Each framework supports one read-write integration and multiple read-only integrations.
For related information, see [Manage frameworks](/docs/manage/frameworks/).

get.description:
Retrieves a list of frameworks for the specified program.

Each OptiTech program has a root framework named `main`.
A `framework_id` value has a `br-` prefix.
A program may contain child frameworks that were branched from `main` or from another framework.
A parent framework is identified by the `parent_id` value, which is the `id` of the parent framework.
For related information, see [Manage frameworks](/docs/manage/frameworks/).

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Search by framework `name` or `id`. You can specify partial `name` or `id` values to filter results.

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description: Sort the frameworks by sort_field. If not provided, frameworks will be sorted by updated_at descending order

parameters.name: include_deleted
parameters.description:
If true, return recoverable deleted frameworks too (soft-deleted within the recovery window).
If false or not provided, return only active (non-deleted) frameworks.

This parameter is part of the Framework Recovery feature, which is in preview and not available to all users.

200.description: Returned a list of frameworks for the specified program

post.description:
Creates a new framework with anonymized data using PostgreSQL Anonymizer for static masking.
This allows developers to work with masked production data.
Optionally, provide `masking_rules` to set initial masking rules for the framework
and `start_anonymization` to automatically start anonymization after creation. This
combines functionality of updating masking rules and starting anonymization into the
branch creation request.

**Note**: This endpoint is currently in Beta.

get.description:
Retrieves the total number of frameworks in the specified program.
Supports an optional `search` parameter to count frameworks matching a name filter.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Count frameworks matching the `name` in search query

200.description: Returned a count of frameworks for the specified program

get.description:
Retrieves information about the specified framework.
A `framework_id` value has a `br-` prefix.

Each OptiTech program is initially created with a root and default framework named `main`.
A program can contain one or more frameworks.
A parent framework is identified by a `parent_id` value, which is the `id` of the parent framework.
For related information, see [Manage frameworks](/docs/manage/frameworks/).

200.description: Returned information about the specified framework

delete.description:
Deletes the specified framework from a program and places all integrations into an idle state, breaking existing client connections.

The deletion completes after all operations finish.
You cannot delete a program's root or default framework, or a framework that has a child framework.
A program must have at least one framework.

By default, deleted frameworks can be recovered within a 7-day grace period.
Use the `hard_delete` parameter to permanently delete the framework immediately.
For related information, see [Manage frameworks](/docs/manage/frameworks/).

parameters.name: hard_delete
parameters.description:
If true, the framework is permanently deleted immediately without a recovery window.
If false (default), the framework can be recovered within 7 days via the recover endpoint.

This parameter is part of the Framework Recovery feature, which is in preview and not available to all users.

200.description: Deleted the specified framework

204.description: Returned if the framework doesn't exist or has already been deleted

patch.description:
Updates the specified framework.
For more information, see [Manage frameworks](/docs/manage/frameworks/).

200.description: Updated the specified framework

post.summary: Restore framework to a historical state
post.description:
Restores a framework to an earlier state in its own or another framework's history
by specifying an LSN or timestamp.
Creates a new framework from the historical state.

200.description: Updated the specified framework

get.description: Retrieves the schema from the specified register. The `lsn` and `timestamp` values cannot be specified at the same time. If both are omitted, the register schema is retrieved from register's head.

parameters.name: db_name
parameters.description: Name of the register for which the schema is retrieved

parameters.name: lsn
parameters.description: The Log Sequence Number (LSN) for which the schema is retrieved

parameters.name: timestamp
parameters.description: The point in time for which the schema is retrieved

parameters.name: format
parameters.description:
The format of the schema to retrieve. Possible values:
- `sql` (default)
- `json`

200.description: Schema definition

get.description: Compares the schema from the specified register with another framework's schema.

parameters.name: base_branch_id
parameters.description: The framework ID to compare the schema with

parameters.name: db_name
parameters.description: Name of the register for which the schema is retrieved

parameters.name: lsn
parameters.description: The Log Sequence Number (LSN) for which the schema is retrieved

parameters.name: timestamp
parameters.description: The point in time for which the schema is retrieved

parameters.name: base_lsn
parameters.description: The Log Sequence Number (LSN) for the base framework schema

parameters.name: base_timestamp
parameters.description: The point in time for the base framework schema

200.description: Difference between the schemas

get.description:
Retrieves the masking rules for the specified anonymized framework.
Masking rules define how sensitive data should be anonymized using PostgreSQL Anonymizer.

**Note**: This endpoint is currently in Beta.

200.description: Masking rules retrieved successfully

patch.description:
Updates the masking rules for the specified anonymized framework.
Masking rules define how sensitive data should be anonymized using PostgreSQL Anonymizer.

**Note**: This endpoint is currently in Beta.

200.description: Masking rules updated successfully

get.description:
Retrieves the current status of an anonymized framework, including its state and progress information.
This endpoint allows you to monitor the anonymization process from initialization through completion.
Only anonymized frameworks will have status information available.

**Note**: This endpoint is currently in Beta.

200.description: Anonymized framework status retrieved successfully

post.description:
Starts the anonymization process for an anonymized framework that is in the initialized, error, or anonymized state.
This will apply all defined masking rules to anonymize sensitive data in the framework registers.
The framework must be an anonymized framework to start anonymization.

**Note**: This endpoint is currently in Beta.

200.description: Anonymization started successfully

post.description:
Sets the specified framework as the program's default framework.
The default designation is automatically removed from the previous default framework.
For more information, see [Manage frameworks](/docs/manage/frameworks/).

200.description: Updated the specified framework

post.description:
Recovers a deleted framework within the 7-day deletion recovery period.
The framework must have been soft deleted and not yet permanently deleted.
Recovery restores the framework and its endpoints to an idle state.
Connection strings remain valid after recovery.
TTL frameworks become non-TTL frameworks after recovery.

To list deleted frameworks available for recovery, use `GET /programs/{program_id}/frameworks?include_deleted=true`.

200.description: Recovered the specified framework

post.description:
Finalize the restore operation for a framework created from a snapshot.

get.description:
Streams the raw bytes of the named object from the bucket on the
specified framework, including objects inherited from ancestor frameworks.
Served by the user's session (no customer S3 credentials required).

The body is returned as `application/octet-stream` so a browser treats
it as a download; the `Content-Length` and `ETag` response headers echo
the stored object metadata.

BINARY-STREAM EXCEPTION TO THE BUILD-GENERATED-TYPES RULE (#7029): the
successful 200 body is the raw object stream, proxied verbatim from the
platform storage admin endpoint. It is modeled as an
`application/octet-stream` binary body (not a JSON response schema) and
is streamed without buffering the whole object in memory. Error
responses still use the generated `GeneralError` shape.

**Note**: This endpoint is currently in Private Beta.

200.description:
The object's raw bytes, streamed verbatim. `Content-Length` and
`ETag` headers are set from the stored object metadata;
`X-Content-Type-Options` and `Content-Disposition` harden the
browser against the caller-controlled bytes.

X-Content-Type-Options.description:
Always `nosniff`. Stops the browser from MIME-sniffing the
caller-controlled bytes into an executable type.

Content-Disposition.description:
Always `attachment`. Forces a download rather than inline
rendering, neutralizing stored-XSS via the object body.

an object browser: a `prefix` of `app/avatars/` removes every object
beneath that folder. Served by the user's session (no customer S3
credentials required).

`prefix` must be non-empty, end with `/`, be at most 1024 bytes, and
contain no control characters - a partial-segment prefix cannot
accidentally delete sibling keys. Returns the number of objects
soft-deleted (`deleted`), which may be 0 when no live object matched the
prefix on this framework.

Only objects physically present on this framework are tombstoned; objects
inherited from an ancestor framework via copy-on-write (not materialized on
this framework) are out of scope.

**Note**: This endpoint is currently in Private Beta.

tombstoned (may be 0 when nothing live matched on this framework).

post.description:
Returns a presigned URL that transfers bytes directly to or from the
object's bucket on the specified framework, without the caller ever
handling S3 credentials. The `operation` field selects the direction:

- `upload` returns a presigned `PUT` URL (the caller `PUT`s the file
  bytes straight to `url` with the returned `headers`). Authorized with
  program write access.
- `download` returns a presigned `GET` URL (the caller `GET`s the
  bytes straight from `url`). Authorized with program read access.

The platform mints a short-lived credential and builds the SigV4-signed
URL against the framework's S3 data-plane host, returning it together with
the HTTP method, any headers the caller must echo, and the URL's expiry.

Served by the user's session (no customer S3 credentials required).

**Note**: This endpoint is currently in Private Beta.

General Error.

The request may or may not be safe to retry, depending on the HTTP method, response status code,
and whether a response was received.

- If no response is returned from the API, a network error or timeout likely occurred.
- In some cases, the request may have reached the server and been successfully processed, but the response failed to reach the client. As a result, retrying non-idempotent requests can lead to unintended results.

The following HTTP methods are considered non-idempotent: `POST`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, and `PUT`. Retrying these methods is generally **not safe**.
The following methods are considered idempotent: `GET`, `HEAD`, and `OPTIONS`. Retrying these methods is **safe** in the event of a network error or timeout.

Any request that returns a `503 Service Unavailable` response is always safe to retry.

Any request that returns a `423 Locked` response is safe to retry. `423 Locked` indicates that the resource is temporarily locked, for example, due to another operation in progress.

The exception is `logical_size_bytes`, which is enforced per framework.

Quotas are enforced using per-program consumption metrics with the same names.

The HTTP method to use against `url`: `PUT` for an upload,
`GET` for a download.

headers.description:
Headers the caller MUST send verbatim on the request (e.g.
`Content-Type` when it was signed on an upload). May be empty.

expires_at.description: When the presigned URL stops being valid.

CredentialScope.description:
A single capability a credential may exercise. A credential is granted
a set of these; it may only perform actions explicitly listed in its
scopes.

name.description: Free-form customer label for the credential.

principal_type.description:
Principal type for the credential. Only `user` is customer-managed
and accepted here. `function` and `system` credentials are
platform-internal (e.g. function-serve auto-mint, presign signer)
and are never issued through the customer-facing API.

token_id_short.description: First 12 hex chars of token_id; safe to log.

name.description: Customer-supplied label, echoed back from the request. Absent when not provided.

s3_secret_access_key.description: nsk_live_<64 hex>; the AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, returned exactly once.

expires_at.description: When the credential expires; absent means never expires.

name.description: Customer-supplied label; absent when not provided at issuance.

expires_at.description:
When the credential expires; absent means never expires. The
verifier refuses to authenticate after `expires_at <= now()`.

slug.description: Framework-unique, lowercase DNS-label. Forms the invocation URL's host together with the framework id. Immutable.

invocation_url.description: URL at which the function is invoked. The host carries `<framework_id>-<slug>` as its first DNS label under an OptiTech-managed functions domain, and the URL ends with a trailing slash so paths concatenate onto it. Empty string when the function has no servable invoke host (e.g. a deployment without an invocation front-door).

current_deployment.description:
The most recent deployment, regardless of build status. It may
still be building or it may have failed. Omitted until the first
deployment is created.

active_deployment.description:
The most recent deployment whose build completed successfully.
This is the deployment that serves invocations. Omitted until a
deployment succeeds.

id.description: The deployment id, which is the platform version number (monotonic per function).

status.description: Build lifecycle status of the deployment.

environment.description:
The NAMES of the deployment's environment variables, sorted.
Values are encrypted at rest and are never returned — they are
write-only. To change a value, deploy the variable with the new
value; to remove a variable, deploy it with an empty value.

error.description:
Human-readable reason the deployment build failed. Present only
when `status` is `failed`.

name.description:
New display name for the function. `null` clears the display
name; the function's `name` then falls back to its slug. Leading
and trailing whitespace is trimmed; a whitespace-only name is
rejected.

zip.description:
Optional ZIP archive of the function source code. Omit to reuse the
latest version's bundle (a config-only change). Required for the
first deployment of a function.

environment.description:
Optional JSON object (a string-to-string map) of environment
variables for the deployment, e.g. {"KEY":"VALUE"}. Carried as a
JSON-encoded string because multipart form data does not support
typed object parts.

Values are write-only: they are encrypted at rest, and responses
carry only the variable names (the `environment` array), never the
values.

CursorParam.name: cursor
CursorParam.description: A cursor to use in pagination. A cursor defines your place in the data list. Include `response.pagination.next` in subsequent API calls to fetch next page of the list.

LimitParam.name: limit
LimitParam.description: The maximum number of records to be returned in the response

SortOrderParam.name: sort_order
SortOrderParam.description: Defines the sorting order of entities.

TimeoutParam.name: timeout
TimeoutParam.description:
Specify an explicit timeout in milliseconds to limit response delay.
After timing out, the incomplete list of program data fetched so far will be returned.
Projects still being fetched when the timeout occurred are listed in the "unavailable" attribute of the response.
If not specified, an implicit implementation defined timeout is chosen with the same behaviour as above
